Fifteen thousand years before the Great Divergence, the Glorious Alliance crashed into the Formingar Ocean — and the survivors crawled out of the wreckage into a dying world. Acid rain. Nuclear winter. Poisoned water. The last great vessel of the rebellion against the Hybrians had become a graveyard scattered across an alien continent.

Knowledge died first. Within a few generations, the written records were gone — destroyed by weather, time, and simple survival. Languages fragmented. The ability to read was lost entirely. All that remained were oral traditions: the stories of the great winged ancestors, of fire from the sky, of the endless walking. They became the foundation myths of every Ge'orian civilization — but they were myths now. The truth of the ship, of the war, of the world they had left behind, was gone.

Then came the dispersal. Over hundreds of years, the survivors found their places. The demons migrated westward, drawn to volcanic lands and black-glass scars — the future Demon Continent. The dwarves went underground, seeking caves and mineral veins. The elves gravitated to the great forests — the Lyrical Forest, the Mystical Forest, the woodlands of Merratodoni. The humans stayed in the central regions, spreading along coasts and plains that would one day become Erisdar. The beastmen found the jungles of Lumina, where strength and instinct ruled. The catmen — as always — went everywhere.

Each species believed it was alone. Each developed separately for nearly two thousand years.

By fourteen thousand BGD, the tribes had grown large enough to meet again. They would not recognize each other. They would not remember the ship, or the war, or the family that had once fought side by side. They would meet as strangers — and the first contact between species would change everything.
